text: Long day over, you're on the couch. Time to relax. Remote in hand, TV on. Now, the biggest question: what to watch tonight?
But before you can even think, a curated list appears. Perfect suggestions, right there. It feels like your TV just read your mind.
How does it know? Is it listening? Or watching you sleep? You might suspect something sneaky, tracking your every move.
It's simpler: the system notes your past choices. It also connects you to millions of others, finding patterns in what people like you enjoy.
The cost? This convenient system can narrow your world. You might miss new gems, trapped in a comfortable echo chamber of what you already know.
Next time you browse, you'll see more than shows. You'll see the subtle blue lines of the algorithm, guiding your choices. Now you understand.
